what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A tour of the ten answers on one graph
sections.para: An invented retailer as one graph, answered by a deterministic engine: where £250k goes and comes from, what recurs and why, acceptances to revisit, cheaper controls, what the business cannot withstand, blast radius, 29 decisions up to the board, and a back-test showing where the model is wrong.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A graph, an engine, plots and decisions
sections.para: Thistlewood is one synthetic graph; each question is a replayable query; each answer shows its plot and proposes decisions with a holder and chain to the board; the back-test shows the model's errors.

sections.label: The company
sections.para: £920k a day at peak through four channels; four board risks over sixteen others, nine accepted; fifteen controls with cost and coverage; 60 humans and 40 agents, one agent of each kind holding only its mandate.

sections.label: 1 and 2: where £250k goes, and where it can come from
sections.para: An extra £250k funds warehouse backups, hardware keys and a second payment provider, cutting expected loss from about £3.5m to £2.5m. Cutting log retention and awareness saves £320k for about £30k of extra risk, each an acceptance with a holder.

sections.label: 3: the five most exposed processes
sections.line: Pick, pack and ship is most exposed
sections.para: Exposure adds security risk to supplier reliability risk. Pick, pack and ship leads at about £1.6m a year, then orders, releases, sign-in and marketing email, each with three costed actions and holders.

sections.label: 4: what keeps recurring, and why
sections.line: Eight causes, and a decision at the bottom
sections.para: 38 incidents come from eight causes, led by credential stuffing, bot surges and expired certificates. Followed five levels down, the last level is usually a decision, such as an acceptance made at an old price.

sections.label: 5 and 6: acceptances whose assumptions changed
sections.para: A competitor breach, a masking rule and cheaper passkeys and keys touch eight accepted risks, each returned to its holder. At flat spend, hardware keys reach 133 of 140 staff and passkeys all three channels.

sections.label: 7, 8 and 10: what fails, and what it costs
sections.para: Ordering, sign-in and fulfilment are minimum viable; warehouse ransomware, through one supplier, costs about £2.3m at peak. Cloud and warehouse outages are the costliest supplier failures, and single points behind every channel.

sections.label: 9: 100 humans and 100 agents
sections.line: Identity admins and deploy agents reach most
sections.para: Blast radius counts systems reachable directly, via others, secrets and sign-on. Identity admins lead the humans; deploy agents reach seven systems, six beyond their mandate; 29 of 40 agents exceed their mandate.

sections.label: The decisions, up to the board
sections.para: Each proposed decision has a holder, door and interval; all 29 reach the chief executive and board, eight via the COO, eight via the CTO, seven via the CISO. Each is a file in the vault.

sections.label: Evidence, and where the model is wrong
sections.line: Measured sources, and a model that is sometimes wrong
sections.para: Answers rest on measured sources. Against last year, two causes are close, supplier fraud is twice the prediction, and four cost far less than predicted, so those answers need recalibrating.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.line: The app, the graph, the engine and the tools
sections.para: The vault holds the inlined app, the graph, the engine, answers, decisions and the build scripts; changing the graph and rebuilding updates everything.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Everything is invented; the model is simple; the courier is not yet a dependency; the twin has 60 humans and 40 agents; nothing calls a model.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: Phil Venables' essay for the questions, and the Thistlewood twin for every number.
